publications.title: Interpreting Latent CoT Reasoning as Dynamical Systems
publications.venueFull: ICML 2026 Workshop on Foundations of Deep Generative Models: Understanding Memorization, Generalization, and Reasoning
publications.role: Co-first author and lead pipeline engineer (Algoverse AI Research Fellowship)
publications.tldr: Latent chain-of-thought trajectories form structured dynamical systems: CODI behaves as a stable attractor, COCONUT as an unstable expanding system, and Sim-CoT supervision tightens both without changing the underlying dynamics.
publications.abstract: Recent latent reasoning methods such as CODI and COCONUT face a fundamental interpretability problem: they carry multiple superimposed candidate traces in hidden space at each step, which obscures how reasoning evolves. We model the sequence of latent tokens as a trajectory in representation space and apply dynamical-systems analysis to characterize reasoning evolution. Using quantitative metrics (step-to-step change, direction consistency, Lyapunov sensitivity) and qualitative projections (UMAP, DMD, PHATE), we show that latent CoT exhibits structured, non-random dynamics with two distinct stability classes.
findings: CODI behaves as a stable attractor: latent states converge into a bounded region, and shorter, simpler paths correlate with correct answers.
COCONUT behaves as an unstable expanding system: latent states spread outward across steps, and more latent work correlates with correctness.
Sim-CoT supervision tightens both behaviours without changing the underlying dynamics.

COCONUT shows three-attractor compression with a mid-chain direction-consistency hinge at step 3, while CODI behaves as a near period-2 oscillator with 85% of samples carrying at least one unstable DMD mode (41% for COCONUT). Signatures hold across GSM8K and MATH.
stats: 22 quantitative plots per run and 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims verified

figures.caption: CODI trajectories projected onto dominant DMD modes contract toward a bounded region.

publications.title: Toward Fairness-Aware Human Feedback for Table Unionability
publications.role: Co-first author, research assistant under Dr. Roee Shraga (BSF Grant 2024022)
publications.tldr: First adaptation of the FairEM framework from entity matching to annotator-level fairness in table union search, showing that human feedback should be treated as conditionally reliable.
publications.abstract: Table union search is a foundational primitive in modern data lakes, and human feedback is increasingly used to supervise it. We adapt the FairEM framework (Shahbazi et al., VLDB 2023) from entity matching to annotator-level fairness and ask whether feedback quality varies systematically across demographic groups. On a 480-row dataset of 60 annotators across 8 questions and 4 survey versions, we find statistically significant disparities that survive multiple-testing correction and five orthogonal cleaning strategies.
findings: 6 of 10 FairEM metrics flag unfairness against non-native English annotators.
25% versus 44% accuracy on hard questions (Fisher exact p = 0.031).
The non-native, lower-education, young triple intersection persists at p_BH = 0.037 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
Robust across 5 of 5 orthogonal data-cleaning strategies; behavioral disparities exceed demographic ones.
stats: 480-row dataset: 60 annotators x 8 questions x 4 survey versions
10,000-shuffle permutation tests and 10,000-resample stratified bootstrap CIs

research.title: Latent chain-of-thought trajectories as dynamical systems
research.role: AI Research Fellow, lead pipeline engineer
research.summary: Selected for the competitive 12-week Algoverse fellowship; modeled latent chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs as discrete-time dynamical systems and reproduced two latent-reasoning training methods end to end on GPT-2.
highlights: Applied Dynamic Mode Decomposition, PHATE, UMAP, t-SNE and PCA to 768-dimensional latent trajectories across 8,792 GSM8K and 500 MATH samples, producing 22 quantitative plots per run.

Reproduced CODI self-distillation (parallel teacher-student with a 3-loss objective) and the COCONUT 4-stage latent curriculum as LoRA adapters (rank 128, alpha 32) on stock GPT-2 with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and PEFT; recovered 99.84% of test samples with a positional overflow guard.

Engineered the reliability layer: a multi-stage Bash and Python orchestrator with CUDA health polling that stabilized 14+ hour training runs, HDF5 resume-from-cache saving about 90 minutes per recovery, a GPU-resident Kraskov KSG-1 mutual-information estimator, and a safetensors-level checkpoint repair that preserved trained embeddings byte for byte.
Built a verification harness that passes 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims on the canonical run.

research.title: FairPrep: demographic fairness for table union search
research.summary: First adaptation of the FairEM framework to annotator-level fairness in table union search, with a complete statistical methodology stack.
highlights: Built 9 source modules across 5 experimental phases on a 480-row dataset (60 annotators x 8 questions x 4 survey versions).

Designed the statistical stack: 10 FairEM confusion-matrix metrics, permutation testing (10,000 shuffles), bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 stratified resamples), Fisher exact tests, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and dual-track logistic regression (scikit-learn for interpretation, statsmodels for inference).
Surfaced statistically significant bias against non-native English annotators on hard questions (25% versus 44% accuracy, p = 0.031), robust across 5 of 5 cleaning strategies.

research.title: Where does physics live in vision encoders?
research.summary: Spatial probing of physical reasoning across the vision encoder, projection and LLM stages of three vision-language models, plus a factorial LoRA ablation to find the leverage point for physical intuition.
highlights: Trained linear and MLP probes on per-patch activations at four pipeline stages of Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL 2.5-8B and LLaVA-OneVision-7B using Physion++ ground-truth physical properties.
Produced physics saliency maps and measured information loss across the projection bottleneck.
Ran a five-condition factorial LoRA ablation (encoder, projection, LLM, encoder plus projection, full model) evaluated on PhysBench, GRASP Level 2 and ConservationBench.

projects.name: Interpreting Latent CoT Reasoning as Dynamical Systems
projects.subtitle: Mechanistic interpretability paper, ICML 2026 FoGen Workshop poster
projects.role: Co-first author and lead pipeline engineer
projects.summary: Treats each latent thought token of a chain-of-thought language model as a state in a discrete-time trajectory and applies dynamical-systems analysis to 768-dimensional reasoning trajectories across 8,792 GSM8K and 500 MATH samples.

pitch.problem: Existing interpretability tools cannot explain how latent chain-of-thought reasoning evolves from one step to the next.

projects.problem: Latent reasoning methods such as CODI and COCONUT keep multiple superimposed candidate traces in hidden space at every step, so existing mechanistic tools reveal compression and shortcuts but cannot explain how reasoning evolves from one latent step to the next.
projects.approach: Model the six latent hidden states as a trajectory; measure step-to-step change, direction consistency, arc length, a Lyapunov surrogate and perturbation divergence; project with DMD, PHATE, UMAP, PCA and t-SNE across four model configurations (CODI and COCONUT, vanilla and Sim-CoT) on GPT-2-small.
highlights: Showed CODI acts as a stable attractor and COCONUT as an unstable expanding system.
Found Sim-CoT supervision tightens both systems without changing the underlying dynamics.
Reproduced CODI self-distillation and the COCONUT four-stage curriculum as rank-128 LoRA adapters with PEFT.
Built CUDA health-polling orchestration that stabilized 14+ hour training runs.
Added HDF5 resume-from-cache, a GPU-resident Kraskov KSG-1 mutual-information estimator and byte-exact safetensors repair.
Built a verification harness that passes 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims.

projects.name: VIO: deep visual-inertial odometry via multimodal fusion
projects.subtitle: Camera plus IMU fusion with a Transformer encoder
projects.summary: Fuses a FlowNet-style CNN over frames, a two-layer bi-LSTM over IMU windows and a Transformer fusion encoder into a pose regressor trained with an L1 translation and SO(3) geodesic rotation loss on synthetic Blender and OysterSim trajectories.

pitch.problem: Synthetic video and IMU streams showed scale drift and domain shift that degraded long-horizon odometry.
pitch.action: Fused a FlowNet-style CNN, a bi-LSTM over IMU windows and a Transformer encoder into a pose regressor with SO(3) geodesic loss.
pitch.change: RMSE ATE fell 31 to 34% versus vision-only, and TensorRT deployment cut per-step latency 35% and VRAM 20%.

projects.problem: Synthetic video and IMU streams showed scale drift and domain shift that degraded long-horizon odometry.
projects.approach: Automated dataset creation and alignment with OysterSim physics and EVO Umeyama evaluation across six training and three test trajectories at 1000 Hz IMU and 100 Hz RGB; compared vision-only, inertial-only and fusion models.
highlights: Cut RMSE ATE versus vision-only about 32% (Infinity), 34% (Random), 31% (Spiral).
Held median RPE near two units across trajectories.
Reached RMSE ATE 7.9 to 12.1, median 7.2 to 8.6, with SO(3) geodesic loss.
Deployed through TorchScript, ONNX and TensorRT: 35% lower per-step latency, 20% less VRAM.
Kept RPE and ATE deltas within 3% after TensorRT deployment.

projects.name: RoboFusion: ML-driven sensor integration for motion control
projects.subtitle: Gesture-controlled robotic arm on ROS2
projects.summary: A real-time human-robot interface that controls a robotic arm from hand gestures by fusing MediaPipe hand tracking, a TensorFlow gesture model and MPU6050 IMU angle estimates inside ROS2, with sub-500 ms gesture-to-command latency.

pitch.problem: Sensor data alone is too noisy and inconsistent for precise robotic arm control in hazardous, manufacturing and medical settings.
pitch.action: Fused MediaPipe hand tracking, a TensorFlow gesture model trained on 5,000+ gestures and MPU6050 IMU angles inside ROS2.
pitch.change: Gesture recognition reached 93% with task precision about 35% above the sensor-only baseline and under 500 ms gesture-to-command latency.

projects.problem: Sensor data alone is noisy and inconsistent for precise arm control, which matters in hazardous remote operations, manufacturing and medical robotics.
projects.approach: Collected a custom dataset of 5,000+ hand gestures with MediaPipe, trained a gesture-and-angle model, fused predictions with MPU6050 readings to cancel noise, and validated in a Gazebo simulation of the arm.
highlights: 93% gesture recognition accuracy on a custom dataset of 5,000+ gestures.
Improved task precision about 35% over the sensor-only baseline.
Held gesture-to-command latency under 500 ms across the full pipeline.
Built production-style ROS2 nodes with deterministic message contracts for reuse downstream.

projects.name: Buildings Built in Minutes: structure from motion and NeRF
projects.subtitle: Classical reconstruction of WPI Unity Hall and neural rendering
projects.summary: Turns uncalibrated photographs into a metrically reliable 3D asset with a full structure-from-motion pipeline, then implements NeRF end to end to render photorealistic 360-degree orbits of the Lego, Hotdog and Ship scenes.

pitch.problem: Reconstructing a building from phone photos for AR and VR needs classical geometry and neural rendering while keeping compute modest.
pitch.action: Built a full structure-from-motion pipeline in OpenCV with bundle adjustment, then implemented NeRF end to end with hierarchical sampling.
pitch.change: Reprojection error fell from 1.75 to 1.01 pixels, and NeRF views reached about 60% higher PSNR with roughly 40% fewer artifacts.

projects.problem: Reconstructing a building from phone photos for AR and VR needs both classical geometry and neural rendering while keeping compute modest.
projects.approach: Phase 1 in Python and OpenCV: SIFT keypoints and matching, eight-point fundamental and essential matrix estimation with RANSAC, PnP camera poses, linear and nonlinear triangulation and bundle adjustment. Phase 2: NeRF with positional encoding and hierarchical coarse-to-fine volume sampling, evaluated with PSNR and SSIM.
highlights: Cut average reprojection error 1.75 to 1.01 pixels across five views via bundle adjustment.
Rendered NeRF novel views at about 60% higher PSNR with roughly 40% fewer artifacts.
Aligned NeRF coordinates to SfM poses for consistent scale.
Added reproducibility guards: fixed seeds, deterministic loaders, metric scripts and result caching.

visual.alt: NeRF rendering of the Lego bulldozer scene from a novel viewpoint

projects.name: TrendED Pathfinder: career recommender
projects.subtitle: NLP role matching and skill-gap learning paths
projects.summary: An NLP engine that matches resumes to roles with TF-IDF and cosine similarity, calibrates rankings with supervised classifiers, and recommends courses that close the skill gaps it finds.

pitch.problem: Job boards filter on job type and company, not on what a specific student can do and should learn next.
pitch.action: Built a TF-IDF and cosine-similarity matcher over 10,000+ job descriptions, 5,000 resumes and 300+ catalogs with supervised ranking.
pitch.change: Match accuracy reached 95% with 90% NLP precision, irrelevant results fell 50% and 1,000+ students used the recommendations.

projects.problem: Job boards filter on job type and company, not on what a specific student can do and should learn next.
projects.approach: Scraped job boards and university catalogs with BeautifulSoup, built the matching and ranking models in TensorFlow and scikit-learn, and generated top-k role plus coursework recommendations from unified text features.
highlights: Scaled to 10,000+ job descriptions, 5,000 resumes and 300+ course catalogs.
95% match accuracy and 90% NLP precision; irrelevant results down 50%.
Cut data preparation time 65%.
Used by 1,000+ students for tailored course suggestions.
Applied LDA topic modeling to job and catalog text.

projects.name: RealmWeaver-AI: procedural game asset generator
projects.subtitle: Stable Diffusion, CVAE-GAN and Wave Function Collapse for Unity
projects.summary: A procedural 2D asset framework that generates terrain tiles and props with Stable Diffusion and LoRA, learns tile structure with a CVAE-GAN, lays out biomes with Wave Function Collapse and places prefabs automatically in Unity.

pitch.problem: Indie developers spend most of their time building game worlds by hand.
pitch.action: Combined Stable Diffusion with LoRA, a CVAE-GAN for tile structure and Wave Function Collapse layouts, placing prefabs automatically in Unity.
pitch.change: Assets reached FID 32.4 at 2.7 seconds each and manual integration effort fell 73%.

projects.problem: Indie developers spend most of their time building game worlds by hand.
projects.approach: VAE-based terrain synthesis, entropy-minimized Wave Function Collapse for biome layouts, LoRA-enhanced latent diffusion for assets, and a classifier-discriminator extension of the CVAE-GAN tuned by ablation for stability and style coherence.
highlights: Beat baseline procedural methods on realism and diversity: FID 32.4, 2.7 s per asset.
Cut manual integration effort 73% with biome-aware prefab mapping in Unity.

visual.alt: Generated 3D terrain tile rendered from the RealmWeaver pipeline

projects.name: SASRec sequential recommender
projects.subtitle: Transformer next-item ranking in PyTorch
projects.summary: A self-attentive sequential recommender with multi-head attention, causal masking and residual feed-forward blocks for next-item ranking, tuned with hyperparameter sweeps and selected by offline metrics.

pitch.problem: Sparse interaction histories make next-item prediction unstable, so the goal was a compact model that holds up under sparsity.
pitch.action: Built a self-attentive sequential recommender in PyTorch and swept dropout, attention heads and hidden size across five variants.
pitch.change: The best checkpoint reached nDCG@10 0.3166 and Hit@10 0.4913 at epoch 14 with two blocks and 50 dimensions.

projects.problem: Sparse interaction histories make next-item prediction unstable; the goal was a compact model that holds up under sparsity.
projects.approach: Swept dropout 0.05 to 0.5, attention heads 1 to 2 and hidden dimensions 5 to 50, visualized stability across five variants and picked the best checkpoint by nDCG and hit rate.
highlights: Reached nDCG@10 0.3166 and Hit@10 0.4913 at epoch 14 with two blocks, 50 dimensions.
Compared five variants by nDCG and hit rate after sweeping dropout, heads and width.

projects.name: Eigenfaces and latent face generation
projects.subtitle: Probabilistic PCA versus beta-VAE
projects.summary: Trained probabilistic PCA and beta-VAE models on 576-dimensional face vectors for unsupervised identity representation and generation, then compared reconstructions and latent interpolations.

pitch.problem: How much of a face survives a 16-, 32- or 64-dimensional latent, and which model interpolates more smoothly.
pitch.action: Trained probabilistic PCA and beta-VAE on 576-dimensional face vectors, then compared reconstructions, latent interpolations and 10x10 sample grids.
pitch.change: Latents kept 95%+ variance, 100 novel faces were generated, and decoder sampling cut training time 35% over dense baselines.

projects.problem: How much of a face survives a 16-, 32- or 64-dimensional latent, and which model interpolates more smoothly.
projects.approach: Reduced to latent spaces of 16, 32 and 64 dimensions with 95%+ variance retained, generated 100 novel faces by decoder sampling, and compared models through PCA-projected visualizations and 10x10 output grids.
highlights: Retained 95%+ variance in 16-, 32- and 64-dimensional latents and generated 100 novel faces.
Found the VAE showed stronger feature continuity and expressiveness.
Cut training time 35% over dense baselines with decoder sampling.

projects.name: Behavioral cloning in Atari Pong
projects.subtitle: Imitation learning with a 3-layer CNN
projects.summary: A supervised imitation-learning pipeline that clones an expert Pong policy from Arcade Learning Environment demonstrations with a three-layer convolutional network.

pitch.problem: Can a small CNN reproduce expert paddle control from demonstrations alone, without reward signals.
pitch.action: Trained a three-layer CNN on expert Arcade Learning Environment frames for 100 epochs and validated with gameplay video logs.
pitch.change: The cloned agent reached 87.55% test accuracy with minimal overfitting and tracked the paddle with sub-500 ms action latency.

projects.problem: Can a small CNN reproduce expert paddle control from demonstrations alone without reward signals.
projects.approach: Trained on expert frames for 100 epochs, validated through loss trajectories and gameplay video logs, and measured action latency.
highlights: 87.55% test accuracy with minimal overfitting after 100 epochs.
Tracks the paddle with sub-500 ms action latency.

pitch.change: Pilot users reported 90%+ satisfaction on a usability survey and TECHVED sponsored the project in October 2021.

projects.problem: Complex indoor spaces are hard to navigate with 2D maps.

Secured TECHVED sponsorship in October 2021 and presented a seminar on AR development tools.

projects.name: shreyaboyane.dev: this site
projects.subtitle: Content-graph-driven portfolio with a depth-map hero
projects.summary: A Next.js 16 and React 19 site driven by one JSON content graph that feeds every page, the JSON-LD, the sitemap, llms.txt and the resume, with a WebGL2 hero rendering a Depth Anything V2 depth map of the portrait.

pitch.problem: The previous site drifted a full degree-completion behind reality because content was hardcoded in four places.
pitch.action: Rebuilt on Next.js 16 with one JSON content graph, a build-time drift guard and a WebGL2 depth-map hero.
pitch.change: One file now feeds 23 project pages, the JSON-LD, sitemap, llms.txt and resume, with every route static and zero runtime APIs.

projects.problem: The previous version drifted a full degree-completion behind reality because content was hardcoded in four places, and its particle background read as a template.
projects.approach: Single source of truth in content/profile.json with a build-time drift guard; Tailwind 4 OKLCH tokens; Motion-Primitives for interactive islands; raw WebGL2 point cloud displaced by depth; static generation for all routes; markdown content negotiation and llms.txt for AI agents; pitch videos rendered with Hyperframes.
highlights: Serves every route statically with no runtime API.
Emits Person and ProfilePage JSON-LD with full sameAs and VideoObject per pitch video.
Keeps one h1 per page and a build-time drift guard on the content graph.
